From theory to practice.

Understanding a concept is one thing. Applying it to a real problem is another. This is where I document practical experiments that connect my learning in mathematics, statistics, data science, and machine learning with code and real-world datasets. Each project is an opportunity to test an idea, make decisions, encounter problems, and understand what the results actually tell me. ### Data Analysis Exploring datasets, identifying patterns, investigating questions, and communicating findings through clear visualizations and statistical reasoning. ### Statistical Exploration Using probability and statistical methods to investigate relationships, test assumptions, and understand uncertainty in data. ### Machine Learning Implementing and evaluating models while exploring how they work, why particular approaches are chosen, and where their limitations lie. ### Experiments & Mini-Projects Small, focused investigations designed to test a concept, compare approaches, or answer a specific technical question. ## Project Journal My projects will be documented as I work through the curriculum. Each entry will focus not only on the final result, but also on the reasoning behind the work. For each project, I aim to document: * *The question:* What problem am I trying to understand or solve? * *The approach:* Why did I choose this method? * *The implementation:* How did I put the idea into practice? * *The results:* What did I find, and how should the results be interpreted? * *The reflection:* What worked, what didn't, and what would I improve? Projects will be added as the work takes shape.
